source_evidence: To avoid buying or selling a stock at a price higher or lower than you wanted, you should place a limit order rather than a market order.
question: Misconception: A market order guarantees that you will not pay more than your chosen price when buying or receive less than your chosen price when selling.
answer: A limit order—not a market order—is the order type the source describes for setting a price boundary. A buy limit can execute only at the limit price or lower, and a sell limit only at the limit price or higher. A limit order may not execute if the market price moves past your limit before it can be filled.
